grades.lower_bound_mechanism: finite transversal + iterated adjoining to force D inside infinitely many minimal supports, then D realized as a term's support (Lemma 2)
grades.upper_bound_mechanism: V as union of multiples of minimal hitting-set radicals; residues mod L; T = #residue classes; window count
grades.notes: (C) proved globally: sequence = increasing enumeration of V from a_1 (eq. 3); Lemma 2 correct. But Lemma 3 (finitely many minimal supports) is gapped: the adjoining process need not terminate—primes outside S can be adjoined forever; the purely combinatorial termination claim is false in general. Periodicity assembly complete and from n=1, conditional on Lemma 3.

grades.lower_bound_mechanism: permanents (minimal transversals): pairwise-intersecting self-dual antichain + killing property forces large primes into permanents with cofactor ≤ a_1, contradiction
grades.upper_bound_mechanism: L = lcm of finitely many permanents, m↔m+L membership invariance, T = count in [a_1, a_1+L), block enumeration
grades.notes: Complete, correct proof. Lemma 1 gives exact enumeration characterization (C). Finiteness of permanents proved rigorously for all terms via Lemmas 2-7 and the antichain contradiction. Lemma 8 assembles global periodicity from n=1 with explicit L (lcm of minimal elements) and T (window count). No false lemmas; nothing left asserted or checked only on examples.

grades.lower_bound_mechanism: minimal-transversal antichain finiteness: killing-property descent (π(d) ≤ a₁p) + pigeonhole on Q with π(Q) ≤ a₁, antichain contradiction
grades.upper_bound_mechanism: S_∞ periodic mod L = lcm of finitely many minimal generators; T = terms in [a₁, a₁+L) window
grades.notes: Complete correct proof. Lemma 1.1 proves characterization (C) for all m ≥ a₁. §§3–5 prove finiteness of minimal generators rigorously via squarefree reduction, pairwise-intersecting antichain, descent lemma, and pigeonhole. Lemma 2.1 assembles full periodicity from n=1: membership invariant under m→m+L for all m, T counts window terms, yielding a_{n+T}=a_n+L for all n≥1.
